description: Authoritative parameters of the audio CONDITIONING sidecar written by the 04_audio stage (scripts/run_audio.py). src/audio/features.py loads this file at import and derives every constant from it. Audio is a conditioning input for models that consume the 63-dim tensor; it is NOT a reconstruction target and is NOT part of schemas/geometry.schema.json's feature vector, so adding it leaves that cross-team contract untouched.

decode.time_source: each decoded audio frame's own PTS on the container timeline -- the same timeline as the video pts_sec in video_metadata.json, so alignment is by absolute time, never by sample position or an assumed common start
decode.av_duration_policy: the video's duration from its own PTS (first frame to last, excluding a final frame reported as tail_frame_gap, plus one median step) is compared with the decoded audio's covered duration; a clip whose two durations differ by more than the tolerance may have its streams misaligned by an unknown amount and gets audio_valid = False everywhere, status av_duration_mismatch. The offset is never guessed. A safeguard: on the 16-clip TalkVid pilot every clip was within 0.06 s (0.03 s after excluding tail-gap frames), and none tripped it.
decode.sync_check_note: diagnostic only, never a gate: cross-correlation of the jawOpen blendshape with audio log energy on a 100 Hz grid, lags limited to a physiologically plausible +/- 0.5 s; a wider search finds spurious peaks at syllable-rhythm periods on 10-30 s clips
decode.discontinuity_policy: a jump between consecutive frames' PTS larger than the tolerance is reported per clip and the samples are placed at their own PTS; the uncovered stretch is marked invalid, never filled

log_mel.frame_time: frame k is centred at audio_start + (k * hop_length + win_length / 2) / sample_rate
log_mel.note: the common 25 ms / 10 ms / 80-mel front end; 100 frames per second

windowing.rule: every features.npz window gets the audio covering [window_time_sec, window_time_sec + window_frames / target_hz), resampled onto that window's own audio grid: frames_per_second * window_seconds log-mel frames and sample_rate * window_seconds waveform samples
windowing.waveform_note: 16 kHz int16 per window, kept so a pretrained speech encoder (wav2vec2 / HuBERT, which needs torch and therefore an env-v0.2) can be run later without re-decoding the mp4s
windowing.validity: audio_valid is false for any audio frame outside the decoded audio's coverage, in a reported discontinuity, or inside a padded video frame; invalid frames hold log_floor (mel) and 0 (waveform) and must be masked, not trusted
